newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer Hi-Bred earnings rise on soybean sales.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Hi-Bred earnings rise on soybean sales.

text.p: Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc. on Wednesday reported higher third-quarter earnings, boosted by strong soybean sales and the robust performance of most of its operations outside of North America.

The seed and agricultural genetics company said it earned $332 million, or $4.04 per share, on sales of $1.3 billion. In the year-ago period, the Des Moines, Iowa-based company earned $303 million, or $3.64 per share, on sales of $1.2 billion.

For the nine months ended May 31, Pioneer earned $285 million, or $3.46 per share, on sales of $1.6 billion. This compared with profits of $258 million, or $3.10 a share, on sales of $1.5 billion in the same period a year earlier.
Pioneer's operations in Europe continued to perform well, paced by strong performances in Italy, southern Europe and central Europe, Chairman Charles Johnson said in a statement.
The company said growth continued in Asia in 1997, while operations in Mexico are making a strong recovery.

This year's fourth quarter will be hurt by uncertainty in sales for operations in Latin America, it said. While long-term prospects are good for that region, 1997 results may be affected by the timing of the supply of new genetics.
Pioneer said its leading North American share of the hybrid corn seed market appears to be 42 percent to 42.5 percent, down 1.5 to 2.0 percentage points from the previous year.
Johnson said fourth-quarter results may not match the fourth quarters of the previous two years, when late planting had delayed some sales to those periods.

Pioneer, which develops and supplies seeds, microbial products and services, said it expects fiscal 1997 earnings to fall in the middle of the range of $2.70 to $3.10 a share. In 1996, it earned $2.68 a share.
Pioneer said it expects to build its North American corn market share in the coming years.

Looking ahead to 1998, Johnson said about 40 percent of next year's corn hybrid sales in North America will be from products released in 1997. In a typical year, about 10 percent of Pioneer's hybrid seed corn lineup is in newly released products, he added.
Pioneer stock fell $4.06 to $72.19 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
